title: An optimized protocol for isolation of hepatic leukocytes retrieved from murine and NASH liver biopsies
protocol: Take liver biopsy from mouse under sterile conditions.
Transfer the biopsy to a petri-dish containing 3 mL ice-cold PBS.
Keep the petri-dish on ice during processing.
Cut the tissue into small particles using scalpels.
Pass digested liver tissue through a 200 μm cell strainer.
Cut liver biopsies into small sections about 1 mm using forceps and scalpel.
Keep tissue in solution all the time during preparation to maintain cell viability.
Further dissociate the tissue by squishing each particle with a 5 mL syringe plunger.
Transfer all PBS and the tissue particles into a 50 mL tube containing 45 mL enzyme digestion buffer.
Incubate for 45 min at 37°C.
Incubate the tissue in digestion buffer for an appropriate time, shaking the tube occasionally.
Place a 200 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL conical tube and rinse with 1 mL wash buffer.
Transfer digested tissue into the 50 mL tube by filtering through the cell strainer.
Gently smash any clumps or aggregates using the flat end of a sterile plunger.
Rinse the cell strainer with 1 mL wash buffer.
Assemble a 70 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL tube and rinse with 1 mL wash buffer.
Filter the solution through the 70 μm cell strainer.
Repeat dissociation by plunger if needed.
Rinse the cell strainer with an additional 1 mL of wash buffer.
Centrifuge the collected suspension at 500 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL wash buffer.
Transfer the cells to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend in 250 μL wash buffer.
Add anti-CD45 antibody (mouse or human, 1–5 μg/mL final concentration) to the cells from previous step.
Mix gently and incubate on ice for 20 min.
Wash by adding 1 mL wash buffer.
Spin down at 500 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend in 200 μL wash buffer.
Add PI staining buffer to the solution (1:50).
Coat a microcentrifuge tube with FBS by adding 200 μL of FBS.
Vortex the tube briefly for 10 seconds.
Discard the FBS from the tube.
Sort the sample using Sony LA900 or another cell sorting instrument.
Recommend sorting by 100 μm chip on Sony LA900 instrument.
Gate on viable leukocytes (PI negative, CD45 positive).
Centrifuge the tube at 500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant until about 50 μL remains.
Add 250 μL of QIAzol to each tube containing sorted cells.
Quickly mix and drop the tubes into a flask of liquid nitrogen.
Store the snap frozen sample at -80°C until all samples are collected.
Thaw the samples from −80°C freezer on ice.
Homogenize the thawed samples by gentle pipetting and transfer them to 2 mL Phase Lock tubes.
Add 50 μL chloroform to each lysate and shake vigorously for 15 s.
Incubate the samples for 5 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase (about 150 μL) to pre-chilled 1.5 mL microtubes.
Add 225 μL Isopropanol to each tube and mix well by pipetting.
Transfer the lysates to RNeasy MinElute spin columns.
Extract total RNA using miRNeasy Micro Kit, with on-column DNase treatment following manufacturer’s instructions.
Use 14 μL of nuclease-free water for elution from leukocyte samples.
Use 30 μL of nuclease-free water for elution from liver tissue samples.
Thaw RNA samples on ice.
Use up to 10 ng of total RNA for cDNA synthesis following SMART-seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA kit’s instructions with a maximum of 10 amplification cycles.
Assess cDNA size distribution and concentration on a Fragment Analyzer using High Sensitivity NGS DNF-474 Kit.
Use up to 10 ng of cDNA to generate the final sequencing libraries with the Tagmentation-based DNA Prep Kit and the IDT DNA/RNA UD Indexes Set A.
Perform index PCR with 9–12 cycles and elute the final library in 30 μL EB Buffer.
Adjust the number of PCR cycles according to the cDNA input amount following Illumina’s Protocol recommendations.
Assess library size distribution and adapter dimer presence on a Fragment Analyzer using High Sensitivity NGS DNF-474 Kit.
Normalize all libraries to 10 nM using Hamilton Microlab STAR Liquid Handling System.
Pool all libraries at equimolar concentrations and spike-in 1% PhiX control V3.
Map filtered reads against GRCm38 reference genome using STAR (v2.5.2b) aligner.
For mapping human sequences, use GRCh38.p14 reference genome as the reference sequence.
Quantify gene expression levels based on genome annotation files from Ensembl version 86 using RSEM (v1.3.0) and featureCounts (v1.5.1).
Use FastQC (v0.11.5), picardmetrics (v0.2.4) and dupRadar (v1.2.2) for quality control.
Perform variance stabilizing transformation using the function varianceStabilizingTransformation from DESeq2 v1.34.0.
Plot VST expression values per sample to ensure comparable count distribution and sequencing depth across samples and sample input numbers.
Perform principal component analysis on VST gene expression matrix using the function prcomp (scale = TRUE) from stats 4.1.2.
Plot PC1 and PC2 to depict sample similarity.
Examine purity of sorted leukocytes by checking expression of liver tissue marker gene Albumin.
Visualize results using ggplot2.
Calculate differential expression between high vs. low leukocyte cell inputs or liver bulk tissue using limma/voom based on mapped counts from featureCounts with a paired donor design in edgeR.
Define genes as differentially expressed if |log2 fold change| > 1 and the adjusted p-value padj ≤ 0.05.
Plot differentially regulated genes to ensure absence of major gene expression changes between high vs. low leukocyte cell inputs.
Use liver bulk versus high input samples as a positive control, which should show over one thousand differentially regulated genes.
